chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Abdul Razzaq ibn Hammam, from Ma'mar ibn Rashid, from al-Zuhri Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Shihab, who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was asked, 'Which of the deeds is most superior in the presence of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no deed after the recognition of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and the recognition of His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), that is more superior than hatred of the world, and indeed for that there are many branches, and for the sins there are branches.'
So the first thing by which Allah was disobeyed was arrogance, and it is the disobedience of Iblis when he refused and was arrogant, and he was from the disbelievers.

And greed, and it is the disobedience of Adam and Hawwa when Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said to them, 'Eat from wherever you wish, and do not approach this tree, lest you become from the unjust.' So they took what they had no need for, and that entered upon their offspring until the Day of Resurrection, and that is that the majority of what the son of Adam seeks is what he has no need for.

Then envy, and it is the disobedience of the son of Adam when he envied his brother and killed him. Thus, from that branched out the love of women, the love of the world, the love of leadership, the love of comfort, the love of speech, the love of exaltation, and wealth. So they became seven characteristics, and they all gathered in the love of the world.
So the Prophets and the scholars, after recognizing that, said: 'The love of the world is the head of every sin.' And the world is two worlds: a world of sufficiency and a condemned world.
ai.seo_question: What is the most superior deed after knowing Allah according to Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) elevates 'bughd al-dunya' (hatred of the world) as the supreme act of worship following divine recognition, framing it as the antidote to the root of all disobedience. The narration traces the genealogy of sin from Iblis’s arrogance and Adam’s greed to Cain’s envy, culminating in the seven loves that converge in the love of the world, which the Prophets and Scholars identify as the 'head of every sin.' This classification underscores the Shia ascetic tradition's view that spiritual success depends not merely on ritual, but on detaching the heart from worldly allurements.

en.hubeali: Ali, from his father, from Ali Bin Muhammad Al Qasany, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Suleyman Bin Dawood Al Minqary, from Abdul Razzaq Bin Hammam, from Moamar Bin Rashid, from Al Zuhry Muhammad Bin Muslim Bin Shihad who said,

‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> was asked, ‘Which of the deeds is superior in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Might and Majestic?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is none from the deeds, after the recognition of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Majestic and Mighty, and recognition of His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup> more superior than hatred of the world, and in that are a lot of branches, and the disobedience also has branches (as well)’.

So the first of what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> was disobeyed with was the arrogance, and it is the disobedience of Iblees<sup>la</sup> when he<sup>la</sup> refused, and was arrogant, and he<sup>la</sup> was from the disbelievers.

And greed, it is the disobedience of Adamas and Hawwaas when Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Said for themas [2:35] and eat from it a plenteous (food) wherever you two wish to and do not approach this tree, for then you will become from the unjust. So theyas took what there was no need with them to it. Thus, that entered upon theiras offspring up to the Day of Judgement, and that is the most of what the son of Adamas sees is what he does not have a need for it.

Then the envy, and it is a disobedience of the son<sup>la</sup> of Adam<sup>as</sup> where he envied his<sup>la</sup> brother<sup>as</sup>, so he<sup>la</sup> killed him<sup>as</sup>. Thus, from that branched out the love of the women, and the love of the world, and love of the government, and love of the relaxation, and love of the speech, and love of the exaltedness and the wealth. So these came to be seven characteristics, being gathered in the love for the world.

Therefore, the Prophets<sup>as</sup>, and the knowledgeable ones<sup>asws</sup> said after recognising that: ‘The love for the world is the head of the sins’. And the world is two (types of) world – the world of the bare necessities and the condemned world ’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali has narrated (from his father) from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani from al- Qasim ibn Muhammad from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari from ‘Abd al- Razzaq ibn Hammam from Mu’ammar ibn Rashid from al-Zuhri Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Shihab who has said the following:

“Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) was asked, ‘Which deed is more meritorious in the sight of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy?’ The Imam said, ‘No deed, after knowing Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, and the Messenger of Allah is more meritorious than to dislike (and hate) the world. It has many branches. Sins have many branches.
The first disobedience to Allah was because of arrogance that Satan committed when he refused boastfully and became of those who reject (the command of Allah).

Greed was the sin of Adam and Eve. Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has said, ‘We told Adam to stay with his spouse (Eve) in the garden and enjoy the foods therein. We (also) told them to stay away from going near a certain tree lest they might become one of the transgressors.’ [2:35] They took what they did not need and this remains in their descendents to the Day of Judgment. For this reason most of the things that the children of Adam want they do not need.

Then it is jealousy because of which the son of Adam committed disobedience and murdered his brother out of jealousy. From this branch comes love for women, love for the world, love for leadership, love for comfort, love to speak, love for higher position and wealth. They are seven characteristics and all of them are gathered together in the love for the world.
The prophets and scholars after knowing this have said: ‘Love for the world is the head of all sins.’ There are two worlds: the world of bare necessities and the condemned world.’”
